title: Payment Service 5xx Spike - DB Connection Pool Exhaustion
description: payment-service returned 5xx errors for 45 minutes due to exhausted RDS connection pool during peak traffic.
root_cause: RDS connection pool max_connections was set to 100 but traffic spike caused 350+ concurrent requests. Pool exhaustion led to ETIMEDOUT errors returned as 503.
resolution: 1. Increased RDS instance to db.r6g.2xlarge (max_connections=1000). 2. Implemented connection pooling via PgBouncer. 3. Added circuit breaker with 50% threshold. Rollback took 8 minutes, fix deployed in 37 minutes.
lessons_learned: Implement connection pooling (PgBouncer) before scaling. Set alert for connection pool utilization > 80%.

title: API Gateway 5xx Surge - Downstream Timeout Cascade
description: order-service and cart-service both spiked to 15% 5xx rates due to inventory-service timeout causing cascade.
root_cause: inventory-service experienced slow DB queries (index missing after migration) causing p99 > 30s. Upstream services timeout at 3s, triggering retries that amplified load 4x.
resolution: Added missing index on inventory.product_id. Deployed in 20 minutes. Enabled retry storm protection (max retries: 2, jitter: exponential).
lessons_learned: All DB migrations must include EXPLAIN ANALYZE before production. Timeout values and retry budgets must be reviewed per quarter.

title: Auth Service 5xx - Redis Session Store OOM
description: auth-service returned 502 errors for 28 minutes as Redis session store ran OOM and refused new writes.
root_cause: Redis maxmemory policy was set to noeviction. Session TTL was not enforced properly due to a bug in session refresh logic introduced in v2.3.1.
resolution: Restarted Redis with maxmemory-policy allkeys-lru. Hot-patched session TTL bug. Rolled back auth-service to v2.3.0.
lessons_learned: Redis maxmemory-policy should always be set to allkeys-lru in production. Add OOM alert for Redis used_memory > 85%.

title: user-api CrashLoopBackOff - OOMKilled after Deployment
description: user-api pods entered CrashLoopBackOff immediately after v3.1.0 deployment. 100% pod restart rate.
root_cause: v3.1.0 introduced an in-memory cache that pre-loads 500MB of user data on startup. Container memory limit was 512Mi causing OOMKilled before readiness probe passed.
resolution: Rolled back to v3.0.9 in 5 minutes. Increased memory limit to 2Gi and requests to 1Gi. Re-deployed v3.1.0 successfully.
lessons_learned: Staging environment must have identical resource limits as production. Load testing in staging must measure peak memory consumption.

title: notification-worker CrashLoop - Missing Environment Variable
description: notification-worker pods crashed on startup after ConfigMap update removed SMTP_HOST variable.
root_cause: ConfigMap update via kubectl apply accidentally deleted SMTP_HOST key (diff not reviewed). Worker panics on startup if SMTP_HOST is empty.
resolution: Restored ConfigMap from git history. Added startup validation to log all missing env vars instead of panicking. ConfigMap changes now require PR review.
lessons_learned: ConfigMap changes must go through GitOps (PR + review). Services must validate all required env vars at startup and report missing ones clearly.

title: search-service CrashLoop - Elasticsearch Connection Refused
description: search-service pods crashlooped after Elasticsearch cluster maintenance window exceeded scheduled time.
root_cause: Elasticsearch rolling upgrade took 2x longer than expected due to shard rebalancing. search-service has no connection retry on startup, causing immediate crash.
resolution: Added startup retry logic with 30s backoff (max 10 retries). Implemented readiness probe that checks ES connectivity before marking pod ready.
lessons_learned: All services must implement startup retry for external dependencies. Maintenance windows must include 50% buffer time for unexpected delays.

title: order-service High Latency - N+1 Query After Feature Release
description: order-service P99 latency increased from 200ms to 8500ms after feature flag enabled for 10% of traffic.
root_cause: New 'order details enrichment' feature introduced N+1 query: for each order (avg 50/page), it fetches product details individually. 50 * 45ms = 2250ms DB time alone.
resolution: Disabled feature flag immediately. Fixed by implementing batch fetch: single query with IN clause. Re-enabled after fix deployed.
lessons_learned: All new DB access patterns must be load-tested. Feature flags must have automatic rollback on latency SLO breach. EXPLAIN ANALYZE required for new queries.

title: recommendation-service Latency Spike - ML Model Cold Start
description: recommendation-service P99 exceeded 5s threshold after HPA scale-out event. New pods suffered 30-45s cold start due to ML model loading.
root_cause: ML model (2.3GB) is loaded from S3 on pod startup. HPA triggered scale-out, and 8 new pods started simultaneously, each downloading the model. Cold start latency was 35-45s.
resolution: Implemented model pre-warming: init container downloads model to shared volume. Minimum replica count increased from 2 to 5 to reduce scale-out frequency.
lessons_learned: Large model files must be pre-loaded via init containers or sidecar. HPA min replicas must account for cold start impact on SLO.

title: product-api High Latency - External CDN Degradation
description: product-api P95 exceeded threshold for 55 minutes due to degraded image CDN causing synchronous waits.
root_cause: product-api fetches thumbnail metadata from CDN synchronously in the request path. CDN provider (CloudFront) experienced elevated latency in ap-northeast-1 region.
resolution: Implemented async thumbnail metadata fetch with 500ms timeout and cached fallback. CDN health added to dependency dashboard.
lessons_learned: External service calls must have timeouts and circuit breakers. Non-critical data (thumbnails) should be fetched asynchronously with fallback.

title: batch-processor Unknown Failure - Silent Data Loss
description: batch-processor silently stopped processing records for 3 hours. No alerts fired. Discovered via user report.
root_cause: SQS dead-letter queue was full (10,000 messages). New failures were silently dropped. No alert was configured for DLQ depth. Root cause of initial DLQ accumulation: malformed JSON from upstream publisher after schema change.
resolution: 1. Cleared DLQ and reprocessed messages with schema fix. 2. Added CloudWatch alarm for DLQ ApproximateNumberOfMessagesVisible > 100. 3. Added schema validation at ingestion point.
lessons_learned: DLQ depth must always have CloudWatch alarms. Schema changes must be backwards-compatible or coordinated with all consumers. Silent failure modes are the worst kind.
